shared_context.content: If x=(x_1,...,x_m) is a vector of length m, define U(x) of length m+1 by U(x)_j = sum_{i=1}^{j-1} x_i and define D(x) of length m+1 by D(x)_j = sum_{i=j}^{m} x_i for 1 <= j <= m+1, with empty sums equal to 0.
shared_context.label: Prefix_suffix_operators

shared_context.content: If t=(t_1,...,t_r) is a sign string with each t_q in {+1,-1}, define x^(0)=x and for q=1,...,r define x^(q)=U(x^(q-1)) when t_q=+1 and x^(q)=D(x^(q-1)) when t_q=-1. Then T_t(x)=x^(r).
shared_context.label: Iterated_operator_for_a_sign_string

shared_context.content: Alt_r^+ denotes the length-r sign string (+1,-1,+1,-1,...) and Alt_r^- denotes the length-r sign string (-1,+1,-1,+1,...).
shared_context.label: Alternating_sign_strings

shared_context.content: For a vector y=(y_1,...,y_m), write Total(y)=sum_{j=1}^m y_j and rev(y)=(y_m,...,y_1).
shared_context.label: Total_and_reverse

strategy_summary: Encode f(s) by the standard dynamic program that tracks the rank of the last entry. The update for the next sign is either a prefix-sum operator or a suffix-sum operator on the current rank-count vector. Prove a general optimization principle for these operators: from any nonincreasing state, the unique best remaining sign string is the alternating one starting with +1, and from any nondecreasing state, the unique best remaining sign string is the alternating one starting with -1. Starting from the first sign and using the symmetry f(s)=f(-s), this forces the global maximizers to be exactly the two alternating sign patterns.
